% Pattern: head/case. The short form of a step of the pf style of proofs,
% \step{label}{statement}, which cheatpf2 defines, heads a case of the proof
% as \begin{step+} does, and with \pfmixednumbers both are numbered by their
% place in the proof. A \step out of a proof is not a case. Seen in the gold
% pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want step--1 other/case 1
% want head-1 other/case 2
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newcommand{\pfmixednumbers}[1]{}
\pfmixednumbers{4}
\newenvironment{step+}[1]{\par\textbf{Step.} #1\par}{\par}
\newcommand{\step}[1]{\par\textbf{Step.}}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem}
Every bounded set is small.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\begin{step+}{step:large}
The set has a largest point.
\end{step+}
 \step{step:bound}{The largest point bounds the set.}
This is the definition of a bound.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
